themes_detail.label: Air Quality Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints spiked to 6 this week versus a baseline average of 1.5 per week—a 300% increase—suggesting a sudden environmental or industrial event affecting Woodhaven/Richmond Hill residents' ability to breathe safely.
evidence: 6 air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.2)
Spike is concurrent with no reported Reddit or news coverage, suggesting residents are turning to 311 as primary complaint channel
High z-score (5.2) indicates statistically significant deviation, not random variation
reporting_angles: Interview residents about what triggered this week's air quality complaints—odors, visible pollution, respiratory symptoms
Cross-reference with NYC DEP air monitoring stations and industrial activity (construction, traffic patterns, nearby facilities) to isolate source

themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Damage Wave
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, damaged street signs surged to 10 complaints (281% above the 2.6 weekly baseline) and curb condition complaints hit 7 (195% above 2.4 baseline), suggesting either severe weather damage, vehicle collisions, or systematic neglect affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: Street Sign - Damaged: 10 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.24, up 281%)
Curb Condition: 7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.4, up 195%)
Both spikes occurred in same 2-week window, suggesting common cause (weather, vehicle impact, or maintenance failure)
reporting_angles: Map the damaged signs and curbs by location—are they clustered on specific streets or routes, pointing to heavy vehicle traffic or a single incident?
Investigate whether DOT has received/addressed related permits or maintenance requests; interview residents about what caused the damage

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting & Litter Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints jumped to 8 last week (392% above the 1.6 weekly baseline) and litter basket complaints hit 3 three weeks ago (1100% above 0.2 baseline), indicating possible gang tagging, commercial littering, or sanitation service breakdown affecting neighborhood appearance.
evidence: Illegal Posting: 8 complaints last week vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.23, up 392%)
Litter Basket Complaint: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35, up 1100%)
Both violations suggest either coordinated illegal activity (tagging/posting campaigns) or systemic city service gaps (trash overflow)
reporting_angles: Photograph examples of illegal postings and overflowing baskets; identify patterns (tags, languages, locations) to determine if organized or chaotic
Interview Sanitation and NYPD about enforcement sweeps; check whether litter basket capacity has been reduced or pickup frequency delayed

themes_detail.label: Public Drinking Incidents Rising
themes_detail.summary: Public drinking complaints jumped 700% to 4 last week versus a 0.5 weekly baseline, marking a sudden emergence of open-air consumption or street disorder that may signal broader quality-of-life decline or enforcement changes.
evidence: Public Drinking: 4 complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.95, up 700%)
Spike is recent and sharp, not a gradual trend, suggesting sudden change in behavior or NYPD enforcement posture
No related Reddit or news coverage implies issue is felt primarily by residents filing 311 complaints
reporting_angles: Identify geographic hotspots of complaints (parks, transit hubs, commercial blocks) and interview residents about visible drinking or disorder
Check with NYPD precinct about recent arrests, enforcement changes, or community complaints; contact local bar/restaurant owners about external drinking

themes_detail.label: Plumbing & Heat/Water Issues
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints spiked 500% to 3 three weeks ago (vs. 0.5 baseline), and heat/hot water complaints remain stubbornly high at 622 over 90 days, suggesting either aging building infrastructure failures or a spike in water-main breaks affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: Plumbing: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.0, up 500%)
Heat/Hot Water: 622 complaints over 90 days (highest non-parking category), indicating chronic winter or year-round issue
Community Board budget data shows repeated annual requests for building/DOB improvements, signaling long-standing infrastructure neglect
reporting_angles: Interview residents in buildings with plumbing/heat complaints; identify if complaints cluster around specific developments or older stock
File FOIL request for DEP water-main breaks and HPD heat violation violations in the district over the past 90 days; check DOB enforcement activity
